basics.name: Mohamed Ibrahim Aljoke
basics.summary: Backend software engineer with 5 years building regulated fintech systems in Go, Node.js, TypeScript and AWS. I own domains end to end: led KYC risk assessment at a Central Bank–regulated fintech (compliance review of new clients from 1–2 days to under a minute) and a credit platform's move to microservices, and took part in the platform-wide security audit and hardening (SSRF, token leaks, data protection, infrastructure). Event-driven design, mentoring, written decisions. AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate.

projects.description: Practice platform for the hands-on CKA exam: a real multi-node Kubernetes cluster (kind) per student to break and fix from a browser terminal, with 203 auto-graded tasks, a timed exam and an AI tutor, on Docker or on GKE.
highlights: Go lab agent runs Docker and kind in a privileged container, builds a 3-node cluster and serves a Connect API, so the same image runs locally or as a GKE pod
On GKE, the platform creates a lab pod per student with client-go, each on its own node from a pool that scales from zero; a NetworkPolicy isolates the labs (tested live)
AI tutor: a Gemini tool loop (Vertex AI) over its own MCP server reads the task, grader and cluster to hint, not solve; RAG over the Kubernetes docs (Ollama, vector + BM25) and LLM-judged evals
Students are identified by token; each one's lab, task state and timed exam are kept apart, and an exam in progress survives a server restart
Browser terminal: xterm.js over a WebSocket, bridged to a Connect HTTP/2 stream into a pty on the cluster node

Task engine runs setup, check and solution scripts on the lab's nodes and repairs what a task left broken; a selftest grades each check before and after its solution. GKE in Terraform; e2e tests run the real server binary
projects.name: CKA Sim

projects.description: Restaurant operations platform built end to end for a real restaurant: offline-first React PWA, Go services and SQS workers, iFood and 99Food integrations, containers on Fly.io and AWS provisioned with Terraform. Private codebase, shown in a video walkthrough.
highlights: Transactional outbox, idempotent at-least-once consumers and one schema per service
Multi-tenant authorization, Redis rate limiting and optimistic locking
Offline mutation queue with conflict resolution and AI-assisted voice ordering
Containers on Fly.io, with Postgres on its own machine and volume, and SQS and S3 on AWS provisioned with Terraform
Point-in-time recovery with WAL-G to S3, losing at most 5 minutes, behind a no-delete IAM user; zero-filled WAL shrinks each 16 MB segment to ~2 KB, so off-site backups cost cents a month
projects.name: Dyosmos

projects.description: Real-time multiplayer game built as a Domain-Driven Design study: rich entities, domain events and SOLID.
highlights: Rich entities and value objects with invariants in the domain, raising typed domain errors and domain events
SOLID: one handler per ability (open/closed), ports and adapters, swappable Express/Hono HTTP layer
Architecture fitness tests keep the domain free of infrastructure; Vitest and Playwright E2E in CI
Optional AI game master on Gemini/OpenRouter with provider failover
projects.name: Social Deduction Game

highlights: Led the KYC risk-assessment domain in a team of 4 engineers, turning compliance requirements into a rules-based risk-scoring engine with weighted scoring and eligibility checks.
Automated the compliance team's risk analysis of new clients in onboarding, from 1–2 days of manual review to under a minute, by integrating 2 external KYC, AML and antifraud data providers.
Translated Central Bank of Brazil (BCB) regulations into product and platform changes; Transfeera is directly regulated, so each new rule ships as engineering work.

Designed a data enrichment engine that picks synchronous and asynchronous steps per client, runs them in parallel, reuses previous results and matches async provider callbacks by correlation ID until a terminal state.

Built bulk reprocessing of existing customers through the enrichment and risk engines, with a leaky-bucket rate limiter that keeps one provider's calls under its requests-per-second limit, ending the HTTP 429 failures at the cost of slightly slower runs.
Reproduced and fixed a concurrency panic in an internal Go proxy (reused fasthttp header buffers) that the bulk run exposed under load, watching queue backpressure and memory in Grafana.
Built automated onboarding and eligibility flows for the BaaS product with domain events, the transactional outbox pattern and asynchronous integrations between services.
Processed account and customer events with AWS SNS and SQS queues, using subscription filtering, deduplication and message groups for ordered, high-throughput delivery.

Designed the onboarding document-upload API in Go: one multipart request for clients, files up to 20 MiB streamed to S3 without buffering, SHA-256 in the same pass and idempotency keys so retries never duplicate.
Took part in the platform-wide security audit and hardening (SSRF, token leaks, data protection, infrastructure) and wrote the team's findings report.

Hardened SSRF protection in the shared HTTP library used by the microservices, covering webhook delivery and intake (to clients and from providers), the reverse proxy, the internal proxy and the downloader for attachments from client links; also fixed a SQL injection risk in the shared library.

Proposed and built an AI-assisted delivery workflow on Claude Code (skills, hooks, one git worktree per repo per task): the agent implements a task, then must pass e2e tests, a local run against mocked providers, a browser check of the screen in real Chrome through the Playwright MCP and a homolog deploy before reporting; it asks at most 3 questions, only on business, money, compliance or irreversible choices.

Built a decision-record MCP server in Go on PostgreSQL and pgvector with hybrid (semantic + keyword) search: agents look up past decisions before changing code and record new ones only with the developer's approval; decisions are superseded, never deleted, and product owners browse them on a web page.
work.name: Transfeera
work.summary: Brazilian fintech regulated by the Central Bank: payments and Banking as a Service

highlights: Led the migration of a B2B credit platform from a regression-prone monolith to TypeScript and Python microservices on AWS ECS and Lambda, splitting onboarding (CAF antifraud, Vindi) from credit; Parcelex and Banco BV sit behind one credit integration layer with fallback, so if one provider can't approve, the request goes to the other.

Designed and built a B2B document-delivery platform over WhatsApp on serverless AWS, chosen because traffic was low most of the time but arrived in sudden bursts (e.g. 23k files at once): files go straight to S3 through presigned URLs so they never pass through API memory, S3 events land in SQS so no file is lost, and a short debounce smooths each burst so it doesn't hit AWS throttling (HTTP 429).

Lambda senders deliver to WhatsApp with retries; files live in their own domain, separate from deliveries, so the same documents serve WhatsApp sends, a chatbot and intake by email, FTP and the web platform, managed from a React admin dashboard.
Coordinated 4 junior developers across 2–3 concurrent projects: technical guidance, code reviews and architecture planning for microservices.

Provisioned infrastructure as code with Terraform, Serverless Framework and CloudFormation, and built CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and AWS CodePipeline, with integration tests using Jest, Vitest and Testcontainers.
Integrated payment providers (Stripe, Asaas, Cielo, Itaú, Mercado Livre) and migrated data from Firebase to PostgreSQL and MongoDB with zero downtime.
Cut idle AWS compute costs by automating EC2 start/stop schedules with Lambda and Slack commands.
Modernized an on-premises delivery PWA in React and Node.js, and built Java APIs integrated with factory conveyor systems, using Redis for caching.
Built a notification client with a webhook system for asynchronous communication between services, improving reliability and traceability.
Contributed to migrating a healthcare management platform from Ruby on Rails to React and Java.
Built SEO-optimized landing pages with Next.js, real-time dashboards fed by webhooks, and a GraphQL layer with Hasura.
